task: Autoregressive decoding with and without KV cache
uncached_method: At each decoding step, the full prompt plus all previously generated tokens is forwarded through the transformer. Attention keys and values are recomputed for the entire growing sequence.
cached_method: The prompt is processed once during prefill. The transformer returns past_key_values, which are passed into subsequent forward calls. Only the newest token is processed at each subsequent decoding step.
prefill: Prefill computes representations for all prompt tokens and initializes the KV cache.
position_handling: The model uses the cached sequence length to infer positions for subsequent tokens. Qwen2.5 uses rotary positional embeddings.
causal_masking: Causal attention prevents tokens from attending to future positions. During single-token cached decoding, the new query attends to previously cached positions and its own position.
cache_growth: The KV cache grows approximately linearly with sequence length. For each transformer layer, keys and values are stored for previous tokens.
correctness: Cached and uncached decoding were compared using exact generated token IDs across three input/output length configurations, each repeated three times.
benchmark_method: CUDA synchronization was performed before and after timing. Prefill and subsequent decoding were measured separately. Median values from three repetitions were reported.
limitations: The benchmark uses batch size one, a Tesla T4 GPU, and short-to-moderate sequence lengths. Speedups depend on sequence length, GPU workload, kernel overhead, and memory behavior. Peak allocated GPU memory includes the resident model and temporary activations.
